transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-03-04
Start time: 16:00 PST
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Sofia Alvarez (Redwood AE), Marcus Chen (Redwood SE), Priya Kapoor (CTO - Nova Tech), Daniel Park (Head of ML), Jamal Reed (Infra Eng)

Summary:
(automatic) Nova Tech is evaluating Redwood for an LLM-powered search and reranking POC. Main decision axis is deployment mode: hosted for speed and iteration, dedicated for predictable throughput, private for strict data residency/KMS. They want clear acceptance criteria (latency, P50/P95, throughput), a reproducible benchmark run, and cost estimates for anticipated 1k-5k QPS burst pattern.

Topics: success criteria, workload profile, benchmarking methodology, timeline, security compliance, fallback strategies.

Action items (recap in call): see action_items field for owners/dates.

Transcript body:
00:00:02 - Sofia: Hey everyone thanks for joining, this is Sofia from Redwood, I think we have the usual crew, Marcus is here on the tech side.
00:00:06 - Marcus: yep hi all, Marcus Chen, infra/serving runtime, I'll drive the benchmarks.
00:00:09 - Priya: thanks, Priya here, CTO at Nova Tech, joining with Daniel and Jamal, we're mainly scoping a POC for search and rerank across our product catalog.
00:00:16 - Daniel: hi, Dan Park, Head of ML. Focus is on quality + latency tradeoffs, we want to see 70-90% reduction in human re-rank time.
00:00:22 - Jamal: Jamal Reed, infra, I'll be focused on network/VPC and KMS stuff.
00:00:26 - Sofia: great, high level we'll walk through workload, acceptance criteria and propose benchmark plan and timeline; feel free to jump in.
00:00:34 - Marcus: quick question on throughput. Priya, you mentioned bursts to 5k QPS — is that sustained or short spikes?
00:00:40 - Priya: mostly short spikes, 10-20 minute bursts during peak campaign windows, baseline steady of ~800 qps.
00:00:47 - Marcus: ok good to know, that affects batching and autoscale config; dedicated vs hosted has different burst handling.
00:00:52 - Daniel: for latency our target is P95 < 400ms for rerank end-to-end including network; P50 < 120ms would be ideal.
00:01:00 - Marcus: noted, with hosted we can probably hit that with optimized model variants and smaller context for rerank, dedicated helps more for consistent tail latency, private depends on your on-prem hardware.
00:01:10 - Jamal: on data, we need to keep some input logs in-house for compliance; what are Redwood's options for KMS and audit logs?
00:01:16 - Sofia: we support customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) for private and dedicated, hosted can integrate with your KMS via key wrapping — there's a SOC2 + audit logs package, I'll share the doc.
00:01:26 - Jamal: sometimes the auto-transcript says KMS, oh sorry; would that satisfy our compliance team for residency?
00:01:30 - Marcus: for strict residency you'd pick Private (VPC/on-prem) where the control plane is in your VPC and data never leaves. Dedicated gives strong isolation but still touches Redwood control plane for billing/ops unless you take the private control plane option.
00:01:42 - Priya: what's the expected unit cost delta between hosted and dedicated? Rough ballpark is fine.
00:01:47 - Sofia: ballpark: hosted higher per-token cost but minimal ops; dedicated moves to committed monthly rate with lower per-token; private has upfront infra + license cost. We'll send a simple cost model; we'll include quantized model options which reduce GPU costs.
00:01:59 - Daniel: important for us is reproducible benchmark; can we get a reproducible workload harness?
00:02:03 - Marcus: yes, we'll provide a dockerized client, workload template and a benchmark spreadsheet. We'll need a representative sample of your prompts and sequence-length distribution to tune batching and kernel selection.
00:02:14 - Priya: ok we'll anonymize; Jamal will send network egress constraints.
00:02:18 - Jamal: yes, I'll produce a 7-day traffic trace and list of subnets and allowed egress if we go private.
00:02:23 - Sofia: Good. Now acceptance criteria — propose we define: 1) P95 latency <= 400ms for rerank, 2) end-to-end throughput handles 5k QPS bursts for 10-20 minutes without >5% error rate, 3) quality measured via regression on test prompts (target no degradation > 2% in NDCG), 4) security checklist (KMS + audit logs) satisfied. Thoughts?
00:02:39 - Daniel: that looks right, add rollout criteria: canary with 5% traffic then 25%, rollback on quality regressions.
00:02:45 - Sofia: yep we'll include rollout plan.
00:02:47 - Marcus: for the benchmark we recommend two phases: baseline hosted run to measure latency and cost, then dedicated simulation with chosen GPU profile for cost/perf comparison, and optional private deployment if residency requires. Each run should be 30-60 minutes with warmup and steady-state measurement.
00:03:01 - Priya: curious about model selection — do you have Redwood-verified models we should start with?
00:03:06 - Marcus: yes we maintain a catalog; we'll suggest a few: a quantized Llama-2 13B variant for rerank, and a smaller 7B variant for quick candidates. We'll surface throughput/latency profiles.
00:03:16 - Priya: if we pick hosted for the POC, will logs be accessible for us? We need sample-level traces for debugging.
00:03:22 - Sofia: yes, hosted provides request/response logs for the POC, you can opt for log redaction or retention controls; but for strict residency we move to private.
00:03:30 - Jamal: about network, if we do dedicated but not private, can we get a VPC peering or direct connect?
00:03:34 - Marcus: dedicated supports VPC Peering and privateLink in certain regions; we'll check region support for your preferred cloud.
00:03:40 - Daniel: benchmark metrics list — please capture P50/P95, tokens/sec, tail lat, error rate, cost per 1000 requests, and model quality metric (NDCG).
00:03:48 - Marcus: agreed. We'll instrument with traces and include KV cache hit rates.
00:03:53 - Priya: timeline: we'd like to have a decision in 3 weeks, POC run in next 2 weeks — is that realistic?
00:03:59 - Sofia: yes, typical: week 1: collect traces and baseline hosted run, week 2: run dedicated sim and private feasibility, week 3: evaluate results and decide. That aligns with your 3-week window.
00:04:12 - Jamal: any pre-reqs from our side?
00:04:14 - Marcus: sample prompts, 7-day trace, SSH or API access for benchmarking endpoint (we can use hosted first), and security contacts for SOC2 docs.
00:04:24 - Priya: ok we'll get that to you.
00:04:26 - Sofia: quick question on failure modes — how does Redwood handle capacity overload?
00:04:29 - Marcus: we have smart routing and fallback policies; for hosted we can route to smaller cheaper variants or degrade gracefully; dedicated gives reserved capacity with burst options, private is up to your infra. We'll show automatic fallback config in the runbook.
00:04:42 - Daniel: any concerns re prompt leakage with hosted? We need to make sure PII isn't retained.
00:04:47 - Sofia: we offer request-level controls: no-log mode, data retention policies, and customer-managed keys. We'll include that in the security artifact.
00:04:55 - Jamal: ok good. Also need to confirm SLA for latency targets if we go dedicated.
00:04:59 - Sofia: dedicated can be SLA-backed depending on contract tier; we'll surface typical latency SLO numbers.
00:05:05 - Priya: ok I'm thinking about decision criteria: if we can meet latency + cost targets in hosted with acceptable data controls, we'll go hosted for speed; if not, dedicated; if legal requires residency, private. Does that sound like the tiered decision tree?
00:05:15 - Marcus: exactly, it's a three-axis: latency/cost, compliance, ops overhead. We'll help map numbers.
00:05:20 - Daniel: one more on benchmarks: please include cold start behavior — we see issues in our existing infra when cache isn't primed.
00:05:26 - Marcus: will do, we'll include warmup and cold-start runs.
00:05:30 - Sofia: any blockers on timelines?
00:05:32 - Priya: only internal legal review for residency might stretch if we choose private but ok for initial hosted baseline.
00:05:38 - Jamal: I'll prioritize the trace and network docs.
00:05:41 - Sofia: great, recap next steps: Marcus shares benchmark template + docker client and cost model by Friday 2026-03-05, Priya sends traces by 2026-03-07, schedule baseline on 2026-03-11. Marcus will run the hosted baseline and share results.
00:05:58 - Marcus: one note: to simulate your burst pattern accurately we may need synthetic traffic generator plus your trace. We'll include a tps script and ramp profile.
00:06:06 - Daniel: ok thanks team, that should cover.
00:06:10 - Sofia: any other questions?
00:06:12 - Priya: none right now. Thanks.
00:06:14 - Sofia: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with docs.
00:06:17 - [call ends]

Notes on transcript: some filler words and auto-transcribe mis-heard 'private control plane' as 'private control plain' in one snippet, and occasional speaker labels folded (e.g., Daniel appearing as Speaker 3 at times).
